title: Rabbi David Tawil: Melachim I Chapter 3- "Shelomo's Wisdom"

chapters.about: Establishing Shlomo's reign and moving into Chapter 3.

chapters.title: Shlomo's Marriage to Bat Paro
chapters.about: Political alliances, building the palace, and the Bet HaMikdash.

chapters.title: The Practice of Bamot
chapters.about: Private altars and the need for a central Bet HaMikdash.

chapters.title: Shlomo's Offerings at Givon
chapters.about: Shlomo loves Hashem and offers a thousand sacrifices at the Bamah Gedolah.

chapters.title: Shlomo's Request for Wisdom
chapters.about: Shlomo asks for a lev shomea to judge the people.

summary: Rabbi Tawil goes through the beginning of Melachim I Chapter 3, focusing on King Shlomo's marriage to the daughter of Paro, his sacrifices at the great altar in Givon, and his famous dream where he asks Hashem for a listening heart to judge the nation. The class explores the balance between Shlomo's political alliances and religious loyalty, the historical context of private altars before the construction of the permanent Bet HaMikdash, and the deep responsibilities of leadership.
questions: Why does Shlomo make a political alliance with Egypt by marrying the daughter of Paro?
What was the significance of the Jewish people offering sacrifices on private altars during this time?
Why did Shlomo go to Givon to offer a thousand sacrifices?
What did Shlomo ask for when Hashem appeared to him in a dream, and why?
